findings.text: every case builds PATH with fake_bin ahead of SHIM_DIR, so the fake is the first lookup hit whether or not real_binary drops the shim directory; I deleted that filter from a copy of reckon/nested_launch.py in a scratch tree and the outside case's assertions still held (returncode 0, same recorded fake path and argv, log reviewer-filter-mutation-demo.log), so the section's "found on PATH after the shim directory is removed" clause has no case that can fail, the self-exec guard that matters once the shim directory is first on a worker's PATH is unverified, and the anchor's claim at :236 that a case proves it is not met.

the refusal's exit status is asserted against REFUSAL_STATUS imported from the module under test at :22 rather than the literal 97 the section fixes, so an edit to that one constant alone leaves the whole gate green while a refusal would exit 0 and a caller could read it as a successful launch; one assertion against the literal would pin the caller-visible contract independently.
